Rashi on Yevamot 21b:10:1.hebrew: ה"ג ואמר רבא וכללא הוא - בתמיה:
Rashi on Yevamot 21b:10:1.english: Thus we read: And Rava said: Is it a general rule? - [This is asked] as a rhetorical question.

Rashi on Yevamot 21b:10:2.english: His mother-in-law's daughter is a forbidden relation - For she is his wife's sister.

Rashi on Yevamot 21b:11:1.hebrew: לאו לאיתויי אשת אחי האם מן האם דבנקבה ערוה - דאחות האם מן האם ערוה, דכתיב "ערות אחות אמך", ודרשינן בהבא על יבמתו בין מן האב בין מן האם. הילכך, בזכר גזרו על אשתו:
Rashi on Yevamot 21b:11:1.english: Does it not come to include the wife of [one's] mother's maternal brother, for in the female [counterpart she is] a forbidden relation - For a mother's maternal sister is a forbidden relation, as it is written, "the nakedness of your mother's sister," and we expound in [the chapter] Haba Al Yevimto [that this applies] whether [she is] from the father or from the mother. Therefore, in [the case of] the male [counterpart], they decreed [a prohibition] upon his wife.

Rashi on Yevamot 21b:12:1.hebrew: מאי שנא האי ומאי שנא הנך - דלעיל: אשת חמיו, ואשת בן חמיו ובן חמותו, ואשת חורגו ובן חורגו; ואע"ג דנקבה ערוה, בזכר מותר באשתו:
Rashi on Yevamot 21b:12:1.english: What is different [with regard to] this and what is different [with regard to] those - [mentioned] above: the wife of his father-in-law, and the wife of his father-in-law's son and [of] his mother-in-law's son, and the wife of his stepson and [of] his stepson's son; and even though the female [counterpart] is a forbidden relative, with the male [relative] he is permitted [to marry] his wife.

Rashi on Yevamot 21b:12:2.hebrew: הא אשת אחי האם בחד קידושין מיקרבא - לגבי דהאי, בקדושין שקדשה אחי אמו. אבל כל הנך דלעיל לא איקרבו לגביה עד דאיכא תרתי קידושין: כגון אשת חמיו — בקידושין שקדש את אשתו נתקרב חמיו אצלו, ועדיין אשת חמיו רחוקה לזה כל זמן שלא קדשה חמיו; וכן אשת בן חמיו — בקדושין שלו באשתו נתקרב בן חמיו, וקדושין בן חמיו באשתו; וכן כולם:
Rashi on Yevamot 21b:12:2.english: This [case], the wife of the mother's brother, is brought close through one betrothal - To this [man], through the betrothal by which his mother's brother betrothed her. However, all those [cases] above are not brought close to him until there are two betrothals: for example, his father-in-law's wife — through the betrothal by which he betrothed his wife, his father-in-law was brought close to him, yet his father-in-law's wife is still distant [unrelated] to this [man] as long as his father-in-law has not betrothed her; and similarly, the wife of his father-in-law's son — through his own betrothal to his wife, his father-in-law's son was brought close [to him], and [through] the betrothal of his father-in-law's son to his wife [she is brought close]; and so too all of them.

Rashi on Yevamot 21b:13:1.hebrew: אשת אחי אבי האב מן האב - דאמרן לעיל: אשת אחי האב מן האם יש לה הפסק, דהיינו היתירא לאשת אחי אבי האב מן האם, דלמטה דידה לאו ערוה היא אלא שנייה. וכי קמיבעיא ליה, באשת אחי אבי האב מן האב, דלמטה דידה ערוה — אשת אחי האב מן האב. וכן אחות אבי האב, בין מן האב בין מן האם, דלמטה דידה ערוה, כגון אחות האב:
Rashi on Yevamot 21b:13:1.english: The wife of a father’s father’s brother from the father - For we said above: The wife of a father’s brother from the mother has a cutoff, which is a permission for the wife of a father’s father’s brother from the mother, since the one below her is not a forbidden relation, but rather a secondary [forbidden relation]. And when he asks [his dilemma], [it is] regarding the wife of a father’s father’s brother from the father, since the one below her is a forbidden relation — [namely,] the wife of a father’s brother from the father. And similarly, the sister of a father’s father, whether from the father or from the mother, since the one below her is a forbidden relation, namely, a father’s sister.

Rashi on Yevamot 21b:13:2.english: Are separate - The kinship has become distant.

Rashi on Yevamot 21b:14:1.english: What are secondary [forbidden relationships] - [This refers to] the baraita above.

Rashi on Yevamot 21b:15:1.english: Secondary [forbidden relationships] of Rabbi Ḥiyya - [Listed] later in our passage.

Rashi on Yevamot 21b:1:1.english: [Is it not] by Torah law - And how did Rav count it among the secondary [forbidden relations]?

Rashi on Yevamot 21b:1:2.hebrew: אלא אימא כלת בתו - וטעמא פרישנא לעיל, לפי שאין בצדה צד כלות דאורייתא:
Rashi on Yevamot 21b:1:2.english: Rather, say his daughter’s daughter-in-law - And we explained the reason above, because on her side there is no aspect of a Torah-level daughter-in-law [relationship].

Rashi on Yevamot 21b:2:1.english: They did not prohibit a daughter-in-law - [This] implies [it] without qualification.

Rashi on Yevamot 21b:2:2.english: The Chaldeans said to me - [These are] the stargazers.

Rashi on Yevamot 21b:2:3.english: You will be a teacher - You will be a sage.

Rashi on Yevamot 21b:3:1.hebrew: ואמינא - אי האי מלפנא דאמרו לי, גברא רבא בתלמוד משמע, אסברא להא דר' אמי — דלא אסרו כלה — מדעתי, ולא אשאלנה בבית המדרש:
Rashi on Yevamot 21b:3:1.english: And I said - If this [term] "teacher" (malfana) that they told me [I would become] means a great man in Talmud, I will explain this [statement] of R' Ami — that they did not prohibit a daughter-in-law — on my own, and I will not ask about it in the study hall.

Rashi on Yevamot 21b:3:2.hebrew: ואי האי מלפנא מקרי דרדקי הוא ולאו תלמיד, אשיילה מרבנן — כלומר, אהיה צריך לשאול, דלא אבינה מדעתי:
Rashi on Yevamot 21b:3:2.english: And if this "teacher" is a teacher of young children and not a scholar, [then] I will ask it of the Rabbis — that is to say, I will need to ask, for I will not understand it on my own.

Rashi on Yevamot 21b:3:3.hebrew: לא אסרו כלת בתו - דהא ליתא בבת צד כלה דאורייתא, אלא משום כלת בנו, דיש בבן צד כלה דאורייתא, כגון אשת בנו:
Rashi on Yevamot 21b:3:3.english: They did not prohibit his daughter’s daughter-in-law - for there is no aspect of a Torah-prohibited daughter-in-law in [the case of] a daughter; [rather, they prohibited her] only on account of his son’s daughter-in-law, since there is an aspect of a Torah-prohibited daughter-in-law in [the case of] a son, such as his son’s wife.

Rashi on Yevamot 21b:4:1.hebrew: כגון כלתה דבר ציתאי - שהיתה לו כלת הבן וכלת הבת ואתו לאיחלופי, וכן כולהו:
Rashi on Yevamot 21b:4:1.english: For example, the daughter-in-law of bar Tzitai - For he had a son's daughter-in-law and a daughter's daughter-in-law, and they would come to be confused [with one another], and similarly [for] all of them.

Rashi on Yevamot 21b:5:1.english: Where there is an aspect of a father - and [therefore] there is reason to enact a decree on account of the wife of [one's] father's paternal brother, [who is forbidden] by Torah law.

Rashi on Yevamot 21b:5:2.english: Or perhaps [it] is no different - [meaning] the wife of [one's] mother's maternal brother [is no different] from the wife of [one's] mother's paternal brother.

Rashi on Yevamot 21b:6:1.english: She herself - the wife of the mother's paternal brother.

Rashi on Yevamot 21b:6:2.english: Is that to say all of them, etc. - This [word] "all of them" is not exact.

Rashi on Yevamot 21b:6:3.english: His mother's mother [is] a secondary [forbidden relation] - Because she is close to a forbidden relation.

Rashi on Yevamot 21b:6:4.hebrew: וגזרו רבנן על אם אביו - שאין בה צד ערוה, משום אם אמו:
Rashi on Yevamot 21b:6:4.english: And the Rabbis decreed regarding his father's mother - in whom there is no aspect of a forbidden relation, because of his mother's mother.

Rashi on Yevamot 21b:6:5.hebrew: וטעמא מאי וכו' - אשת אבי אביו שנייה, שסמוכה לאשת אב:
Rashi on Yevamot 21b:6:5.english: And what is the reason, etc. - [His] father's father's wife is a secondary [forbidden relation], because she is close to [his] father's wife.

Rashi on Yevamot 21b:7:1.hebrew: וגזרו רבנן על אשת אבי אמו - אע"ג דלא שייך צד אישות אב דאורייתא לא למעלה ולא למטה, משום אשת אבי אביו:
Rashi on Yevamot 21b:7:1.english: And the Sages decreed regarding his mother’s father’s wife - Even though the aspect of a father’s marriage [prohibited by] Torah law does not apply, neither upward nor downward, [they decreed regarding her] because of his father’s father’s wife.

Rashi on Yevamot 21b:8:1.hebrew: <abbr title="הכי גרסינן">ה"ג</abbr>: כולהו דבי דודי קרו לה, <abbr title="ולא גרסינן">ול"ג</abbr> רבתי:
Rashi on Yevamot 21b:8:1.english: This is the [correct] reading: "They all call her [of] the house of the uncle," and we do not read "rabbati."

Rashi on Yevamot 21b:9:1.hebrew: כל שבנקבה ערוה - שאם היתה נקבה היתה ערוה לזה, גזרו בזכר על אשתו. וכולהו מפרש ואזיל להו:
Rashi on Yevamot 21b:9:1.english: Any [relative] that in a female is a forbidden relation - That if [that relative] were a female, she would be a forbidden relation to this [person], they decreed regarding a male [relative] upon his wife. And he goes on to explain all of them.

Tosafot on Yevamot 21b:13:1.hebrew: אשת אחי אבי האב ואחות אבי האב מהו - הוה מצי למיבעי אחות אם האם, והיא בכלל אחות אבי האב דלמטה דידה ערוה; ואית ספרים דגרסינן לה בהדיא:
Tosafot on Yevamot 21b:13:1.english: What is [the law regarding] the wife of a father's father's brother and the sister of a father's father? - [The Gemara] could also have asked [about] the sister of a mother's mother, and it is included in [the category of] the sister of a father's father, since [one generation] below her is a forbidden relation; and there are texts in which we read it explicitly.

Tosafot on Yevamot 21b:15:1.hebrew: מאי שייר דהאי שייר - אף על גב דתרתי נינהו, חדא חשיב להו, כדקאמר בסמוך: "הנהו תרתי דדמיין להדדי — חדא חשיב להו". ופירש בקונטרס דהנך תרתי היינו אשת אחי אבי האב ואחות אבי האב; ולא כמו שפירש רבינו יצחק בן רבינו מאיר דקאי אאשת אחי האם מן האם ואשת אחי האם מן האב, דכולהו "אחי אמו" קרו להו:
Tosafot on Yevamot 21b:15:1.english: What [else] did he omit that he omitted this - Even though there are two [cases], he counts them as one, as [the Gemara] says shortly: "Those two that are similar to each other — he counts them as one." And Rashi explained that those two are the wife of the father's father's brother and the sister of the father's father's brother; and not as Rabbeinu Yitzchak ben Rabbeinu Meir explained, that it refers to the wife of the mother's maternal brother and the wife of the mother's paternal brother, since all of them are called "his mother's brother."

Tosafot on Yevamot 21b:16:1.hebrew: אמימר אכשר כו' - פסק רבינו חננאל דהלכה כאמימר, וכן בשאלתות דרב אחאי, וכן משמע דסבר רב אשי, דקאמר: "השתא נמי דכתיבי לאיסורא, לאו מר בריה דרבנא חתים עלייהו". ולר"י נראה דאין הלכה כאמימר, דסוגיא דגמרא בהחולץ (לקמן יבמות דף מ: ושם) דלא כוותיה; וקאמר נמי אמימר מוקי לה משום חולץ, וקסבר גזרו שניות בחלוצה, ואין התלמוד רוצה לפשוט בעיא שלו מדברי אמימר:
Tosafot on Yevamot 21b:16:1.english: Ameimar permitted, etc. - Rabbeinu Chananel ruled that the halakhah is in accordance with Ameimar, and so [too is it ruled] in the She'iltot of Rav Achai, and so it seems that Rav Ashi holds, as he says: "Even now that they are written as forbidden, Mar son of Rabbana is not signed on them." But to the Ri it appears that the halakhah is not in accordance with Ameimar, for the Talmudic passage in [chapter] HaCholetz (below, Yevamot 40b, and see there) is not in accordance with him; and it also says [there] that Ameimar establishes it because of one who performs chalitzah, and he holds that [the Sages] decreed secondary forbidden relationships in the case of a chalutzah, and the Talmud does not want to resolve its inquiry from the words of Ameimar.

Tosafot on Yevamot 21b:3:1.hebrew: לא אסרו כלת בתו אלא משום כלת בנו - ותימה, דאמאי לא אסרינן לה משום "כל שבנקבה ערוה, בזכר גזרו על אשתו משום שנייה" כדלקמן? דטעם גמור הוא ולא סימנא בעלמא, מדפריך עלה: "מ"ש הני ומ"ש הני? הא בחד קדושי מקרב לה כו'". ועוד: מדפשיט מינה אשת אחי האם מן האם, ולא מוקי לה בכלת בתו! ואור"י, דתנא דברייתא לית ליה ההוא טעמא, אבל בדורות האחרונים גזרו; ולהכי כי פריך "מאי שייר דהאי שייר?", לא בעי למימר דשייר אשת אחי האם מן האם, דפשטנא לאיסור'. ואם תאמר: מאי פריך "וכללא הוא? חמותו ערוה כו'"? דלמא בהני נמי גזרו בתר הכי מהאי טעמא! וי"ל, דקים ליה בהנהו דשרו. והא דפריך לקמן "וליטעמיך שבסרי הויין?", אע"ג דבתר הכי גזרו כדפי', יודע הוא דשניות דמר בריה דרבנא בדורות אחרונים הוה:
Tosafot on Yevamot 21b:3:1.english: They prohibited his daughter's daughter-in-law only due to his son's daughter-in-law - And it is astonishing: why do we not prohibit her because of [the principle] "Any [relationship] that in a female is a forbidden relation, in a male they decreed upon his wife as a secondary [forbidden] relation," as [stated] below? For it is a full-fledged reason and not merely a mnemonic, [as is evident] from the fact that [the Gemara] objects to it: "What is different [about] these and what is different [about] these? This [one] is related by a single [act of] betrothal, etc." And furthermore, from the fact that [the Gemara] resolves from it [the case of] the wife of the mother's maternal brother, and does not establish it as [referring to] his daughter's daughter-in-law! And R"I says that the Tanna of the baraita does not hold that reason, rather in later generations they decreed [it]; and therefore, when [the Gemara] asks "What [else] did he omit that he omitted this?", it does not want to say that he omitted the wife of the mother's maternal brother, which we resolved to be prohibited. And if you ask: Why does [Rava] ask "Is it a [general] principle? His mother-in-law is a forbidden relation, etc."? Perhaps regarding these [cases] as well they decreed afterwards for this reason! And one can answer that he was certain regarding those [cases] that they are permitted. And [as for] that which [the Gemara] asks below "And according to your reasoning, there are seventeen!" — even though they decreed [it] afterwards as I explained, he knows that the [list of] secondary relations of Mar son of Rabbana was in later generations:

Tosafot on Yevamot 21b:4:1.hebrew: רב אשי אמר כגון כלה דבי רב מרי בר איסק - כל חד נקיט אותו שהיה בימיו, וצ"ל דתרי מרי בר איסק הוו: אחד בימי רב אשי, כדמשמע הכא, ובפרק אלו מציאות (ב"מ דף כב.): "אמימר ורב אשי ומר זוטרא איקלעו לבוסתני' דבי מרי בר איסק". ואחד היה בימי רב חסדא, דאמר בהמפקיד (שם דף לט: ושם): "מרי בר איסק — ואיכא דאמרי חנה בר איסק — אתא ליה אחוה מבי חוזאי, אתא לקמיה דרב חסדא". ורב חסדא נפטר בימי רבא, כדאמר בפ' בתרא דיומא (ד' עה: ושם), וביום שמת רבא נולד רב אשי, כדאיתא בפרק עשרה יוחסין (קידושין דף עב:):
Tosafot on Yevamot 21b:4:1.english: Rav Ashi said: For example, the daughter-in-law of the house of Rav Mari bar Isak - Each one mentioned [a household] that existed in his days, and one must say that there were two [people named] Mari bar Isak: one in the days of Rav Ashi, as is implied here, and in the chapter [entitled] Eilu Metziot (Bava Metzia 22a): "Ameimar, Rav Ashi, and Mar Zutra visited the orchard of the house of Mari bar Isak." And one was in the days of Rav Chisda, as [the Gemara] says in [the chapter entitled] HaMafkid (ibid. 39b, and elsewhere): "Mari bar Isak — and some say Chanah bar Isak — his brother came to him from Bei Chozai; he came before Rav Chisda." And Rav Chisda passed away in the days of Rava, as [the Gemara] says in the last chapter of Yoma (75b, and elsewhere), and on the day that Rava died, Rav Ashi was born, as is stated in the chapter [entitled] Asarah Yuchasin (Kiddushin 72b).
